[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Dockerizing Selenium Grid & Scaling Containers"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Selenium Grid allows you to run test scripts on various machines against different browsers concurrently. By containerizing Selenium Grid using Docker, you can provision test environments dynamically, ensure consistency, and easily scale worker nodes up or down."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Docker and Docker Compose installed on your local machine or CI/CD server."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic knowledge of Selenium WebDriver and Docker concepts."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating the Docker Compose File"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The cleanest way to orchestrate a Selenium Grid with a Hub and browser nodes is using Docker Compose. Create a file named docker-compose.yml in your project directory."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"version: "3"
services:
  selenium-hub:
    image: selenium/hub:latest
    container_name: selenium-hub
    ports:
      - "4444:4444"

  chrome:
    image: selenium/node-chrome:latest
    depends_on:
      - selenium-hub
    environment:
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_HOST=selenium-hub
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_PUBLISH_PORT=4442
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_SUBSCRIBE_PORT=4443

  edge:
    image: selenium/node-edge:latest
    depends_on:
      - selenium-hub
    environment:
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_HOST=selenium-hub
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_PUBLISH_PORT=4442
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_SUBSCRIBE_PORT=4443"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Running and Scaling the Grid"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"To spin up the hub and single nodes, run the following command in your terminal:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"docker-compose up -d"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"To scale up your Chrome testing capacity dynamically, you can use the --scale flag with Docker Compose without modifying the configuration file."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"docker-compose up --scale chrome=3 -d"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command provisions three independent Chrome node containers, instantly increasing parallel test execution capacity."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Verifying the Grid"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the containers are running, navigate to http://localhost:4444 in your web browser. You will see the Selenium Grid UI displaying the registered nodes and available browser slots ready to accept remote WebDriver sessions."}]
